_comment: Phase-4 E02: region-code -> consumer-branch binding, decoded from the committed byte-verified hand-asm (v5 corpus) + committed live proofs. Companion census: analysis/phase4_e02_region_code_census.json.

query.reads: gate byte (caller-supplied, must == 1) -> G_CUR_SECTOR [0x80090560 + idx*20] -> code s16 [0x800A7E48 + sector*0x30 + 0x2E]

branches.0: no-op (also returned when the flik gate != 1)
branches.1: FUNC_8004A700(0, 0, sp+44, a3=1) -- transition initiator variant A (.L_800496A8); sets the handled flag
branches.3: .L_800496E8: [0x800823A0]=1, fade [0x80082470]=23, FUNC_80050994(58,0) via the shared tail .L_80049700 -- a SECOND exit-code value. ⚠️ NOT identical to code 2: the code-2 arm additionally stores the position-commit flag sp+0x50=1 and code 3 does not, so at the join .L_80049748 code 2 re-commits position and clears player+0x82 while code 3 leaves both. Shared EFFECT, different ARMS.
branches.4: .L_80049718: gated on player+0x7E==0 AND player+0x92==0, then FUNC_8004A700(0, 0, sp+44, a3=0) -- transition variant B
branches.>=5: falls to the common tail -- no consumer (and the unfiltered census proves no such codes exist in retail data)

player_dispatch_0x80048138.first_call_site_note: an earlier call site (~line 1422) uses the query only as a zero/nonzero gate combined with three player velocity fields

code3_correction_2026_08_11.superseded_text: .L_800496E8: IDENTICAL body to code 2 via the shared tail .L_80049700 -- a SECOND exit-code value
code3_correction_2026_08_11.why: Body-level reading. An instruction-level decode shows the writes to sp+0x50 are an exact set of three -- 0x800481BC zero-init, 0x800496C0 (code-1 arm), 0x800496E4 (code-2 arm) -- with one read at 0x80049748. Codes 3 and 4 never set it.
code3_correction_2026_08_11.authority: analysis/phase4_f01_objective_lifecycle.json and the Canon exit-trigger matrix; the disagreement was caught by the F04 row assessment, which found F04 inheriting the older of two pinned artifacts.
code3_correction_2026_08_11.unaffected: E02's census and its live be-here proofs stand -- both arms produce the exit effect, so code 3 remains live-proven. Only the 'identical body' phrasing was wrong.

checkpoint_save_0x80054C90.behavior: after a state gate via 0x80038F84, queries the code and BAILS if code == 4: standing in a code-4 sector suppresses checkpoint/respawn-anchor saving (dovetails with C15 safe-anchor canon)

mover_actor_update_0x8004B940.behavior: queries with the object's own gate byte (+0x5E); if code == 1: stores +0x5A=0, +0x62=2, +0x6E=0 on the object -- +0x6E is the pool-actor HP offset, so actors in a code-1 sector are retired (state 2). Measured stores; role naming is offset-based inference.
mover_actor_update_0x8004B940.tier: static_decoded; semantics inferred from confirmed +0x6E=HP layout

code_semantics_summary.1: pre-exit/transition band (player: FUNC_8004A700 variant A; actors: retirement) -- census shows code-1 bands leading INTO ending sectors (tunnels 570-578, riverbed_run 292-296, city_entrance 219)

code_semantics_summary.4: no-checkpoint zone (checkpoint_save bail) + state-gated transition variant B (city_entrance 220-225)
